elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 5.4: "IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL". The element is disjunctive, so a right reaching the Agreement itself suffices; the pre-existing PO cancellation right (p0722) is additional, not required. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returns false only because the rendered phrasing is "terminate this Agreement for its convenience" (interposed "its"); in substance the operative right is present and runs in Customer's favour.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL" - 30 days, written, no additional conditions or Vendor consent.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination" - the word "pro rata" is express, not inferred from the post-termination period alone, and the payer direction is Vendor-to-Customer.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 5.1 preamble limits exit to cause: "this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows", and Section 4.0 permits termination during the initial three-year term only "as provided in Section 5.0". Section 4.0's six (6) months' notice operates against automatic renewal and is scored under RENEWAL, not as a mid-term Vendor convenience right. The new 5.4 grants the convenience right to IBM only and creates no reciprocal MSL right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 sets thirty (30) days, which is better than fallback but outside the 60-90 day band; the fallback level is therefore not the level satisfied.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No fee cap appears anywhere; the retained cost-reimbursement mechanics (p0722 "shall not relieve IBM of any cost reimbursements under the Price section" and the Parts cost provision at p0143) remain uncapped. To reach the fallback the drafter would have to add an express cap of three (3) months' fees on any charge payable on convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.0 lets "either Party" give six (6) months' written notice "of its intent to terminate this Agreement" without expressly tying the effective date to the end of the then-current renewal term; per the rule boundary, such an auto-renewal notice mechanic does not establish term-end-only Vendor termination. (Immaterial here because the preferred level is complete.)

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition is effectively inapplicable: MSL has no mid-term convenience right, and the only notice-based exit available to MSL (Section 4.0) requires six (6) months' notice, comfortably exceeding 90 days.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the inserted Section 5.4 supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and the retained for-cause-only Section 5.0 already denies MSL any mid-term convenience exit, so no new restriction on MSL was needed or drafted.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, no survival tail, expense allocation, damages category, or procedure is bolted on, and the T4C-surplus phrase "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted since the selected checklist and the Agreement's Purchase Order cancellation right (p0722) do not require a partial-termination structure.

The narrow "Notwithstanding Section 5.1" opener is justified rather than a broad override: Section 5.1's own preamble reads "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows", which would otherwise contradict the new clause. The reference resolves to the heading at p0106, so it is not dangling.

Intent preserved: the for-cause grounds, the three-year term, the Section 4.0 renewal/non-renewal mechanic, the Purchase Order cancellation right, and the Parts cost-reimbursement pricing (p0143) all survive without contradiction, because the override is limited to Section 5.1.

Residual point to verify before sending (not a defect in the drafted language): confirm that "5.4" is an unused number within Section 5.0, which appears to run through several subsections (p0107-p0118); renumber if it collides.

Note for negotiation, not a checklist failure: retained p0722 and the Parts cost provision mean a convenience exit may still carry cost reimbursements. If the counterparty pushes us to the fallback (60-90 days), we would then also need an express cap of three (3) months' fees on those charges to make the fallback level complete.
